claims.text: The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are solid, single-phase crystalline particles with a homogeneous elemental distribution.
Premelting and melting progression is governed by thermally activated surface segregation of Cu.
Cu has a lower melting point than the other FeNiCrCoCu constituents.
Elevated temperature preferentially increases the surface mobility of Cu atoms.
Preferential Cu mobility produces a Cu-enriched, liquid-like surface layer.
The Cu-rich surface layer locally depresses the effective melting temperature.
The locally depressed surface region nucleates a transformation that propagates inward through the nanoparticle.
The proposed controlled comparison heats standard-composition and reduced-Cu nanoparticles at approximately 10 K/min under inert conditions.
The comparison uses nanoparticles with an average size of approximately 50 nm and a narrow size distribution.
Below the premelting onset, the nanoparticles remain fully crystalline and compositionally uniform.
Below the premelting onset, the nanoparticles have high mechanical stiffness.
At an onset temperature, in-situ TEM and EDS will reveal a thin Cu-rich, liquid-like surface shell before complete melting.
Formation of the surface shell will coincide with decreased mechanical stiffness.
The transition will produce an exothermic DSC signal.
Reducing Cu content will raise the onset temperature of surface premelting.
Reducing Cu content will make the melting transition more spatially uniform.
The hypothesis is restricted to non-oxidizing conditions, narrow particle-size distributions, and heating rates that avoid thermal shock or anomalous diffusion.
Absence of a Cu-enriched liquid-like surface layer before complete melting, together with no surface-initiated thermal or mechanical change, would falsify the hypothesis.
